name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,155

clue.text: Romanians resettled in European country

indicators.note: people who are resettled are moved to new places, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, all nine letters used

explanation.surface: A group of Romanian migrants settles down in another European nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The nationality is not a hint at Romania itself: its nine letters exactly rebuild the name of the tiny republic.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a microstate enclosed by Italy, one of the smallest independent nations in Europe.

clue.text: Diseased lake abandoned in oil spillage

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so that letter drops out of the longer word

blocks.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
an oil slick is a layer of spilled oil on water

explanation.surface: A lake has been left polluted and diseased by an oil spill.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of SLICK to leave SICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a body or organism that is unwell and suffering from illness.

clue.text: Rising brown river following the usual course

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upward, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Ural is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A river swollen with brown water flows along its normal path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like it describes the river in flood, but it only turns the colour upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something natural happens as expected, in line with the ordinary run of events, without interference.

clue.text: Duo skipping piano melody

indicators.note: to skip something is to leave it out, so one letter is omitted

blocks.note: a duo is a pair
p is the musical marking for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Two musicians perform a tune without the piano part.
explanation.walkthrough: PAIR without P leaves the answer; piano and melody both keep the surface musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is an old word for a tune or song, especially a simple one.

clue.text: Popular worker already being dealt with

blocks.note: something in is fashionable
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A well-liked employee already has the task under way.
explanation.walkthrough: IN for popular and HAND for worker are both standard crossword equivalences.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a matter under control and currently receiving attention, so nobody else needs to take it up.

clue.text: Polluted water for children?

blocks.note: food or drink that is off has gone bad
a spring is a natural source of water

explanation.surface: Is this contaminated water suitable for kids to drink?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Polluted water' is not about drinking: it splits into two words that join into a word for descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's or animal's young, their sons and daughters collectively.

clue.text: Article subsequently trimmed

indicators.note: a trimmed word has had its end cut off, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: afterwards, subsequently

explanation.surface: A piece of writing was later edited down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads like a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article; THEN loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The is the English definite article, the grammatical term for words like a, an and the.

clue.text: Vagrant heading for trouble on freeway exit?

indicators.note: the heading of anything is its top, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of trouble
an off-ramp is the sloping road leaving a freeway

explanation.surface: A homeless wanderer heads for a highway off-ramp, looking for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A freeway is a North American motorway, and its exits are ramps.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless person who travels about on foot, which is what a vagrant is.

clue.text: Learn to manoeuvre around front half of this entrance

indicators.note: to manoeuvre is to steer and reposition, so the letters are moved around
going around something means enclosing it, so one piece is wrapped round the other
the front half of a four-letter word is its first two letters only

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the first two of its four letters, the front half of the word

explanation.surface: A learner driver is told to steer around the front of this entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' reads as a doorway, but it is the verb meaning to put someone in a trance, and the stress moves to its second syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance and to enthral both mean to captivate someone completely, holding their attention spellbound.

clue.text: Confused chart about a source of regular cold symptom

indicators.note: confused means muddled up, so the letters are jumbled
about means surrounding, so one set of letters goes around another
the source of something is where it begins, so its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
the first letter of regular

explanation.surface: A confusing medical chart describes a common symptom of colds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular' is not a medical word here: only its first letter is used, and 'cold symptom' is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is the build-up of mucus in the nose and throat that accompanies a common cold.

clue.text: Fine bridge player in celebration

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
the four bridge players are named North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: A skilled card player takes part in a party.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the seats are compass points, so any of N, S, E or W, or the full words, can stand for a player.
explanation.definitionFit: A feast is a large celebratory meal or a religious festival, both kinds of celebration.

clue.text: Material for correspondents? Initially we telephone Times, say, about it

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter is kept
about means around, so one word is placed around the other

blocks.note: the first letter of we
to ring someone is to telephone them
taken as written
The Times is an example of a newspaper, as 'say' signals

explanation.surface: Journalists phone the Times newsroom about a story they are filing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondents' suggests reporters, but here it means letter-writers; the Times is a British newspaper, given as an example by 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is stationery used for letters, the material people who correspond by post write on.

clue.text: Cutting insect at bottom of ditch

indicators.note: in a down entry, being at the bottom means coming after the other part

blocks.note: a trench is a long narrow ditch
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect crawls along the bottom of a drainage channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' could be a railway cutting, close to a ditch, but it is the adjective for sharp remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant criticism is incisive and sharp, so it is cutting in the figurative sense of wounding words.

clue.text: Official accepting story in mitigation

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: a ref, short for referee, is a sports official
a story can be a lie, a made-up tale

explanation.surface: A referee accepts a player's excuse as grounds for leniency.
explanation.walkthrough: Story as a fib is a common crossword sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is the easing of pain or hardship, which is what mitigation means: making something less severe.

clue.text: Nonsense about small drink where speaker stands

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around another

blocks.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
rum is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone talks rubbish about having had a small drink at the lectern.
explanation.walkthrough: S for small is the clothing-size abbreviation, and 'about' wraps only the nonsense word around it before the drink is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform from which a lecturer or orator addresses an audience.

clue.text: Daughter is married, almost entirely unhappy

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for married
entirely means all of it

explanation.surface: A daughter has got married and is nearly completely miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: D and M are standard genealogical abbreviations; ALL loses its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means gloomy and depressing, so a dismal person or mood is sad and cheerless.

clue.text: Not entirely crazy about family’s audacious swimwear

indicators.note: not entirely means falling just short of the whole, so the final letter goes
about means around, so one word wraps another

blocks.note: manic means wildly frenzied, crazy
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A slightly mad relative wears daring beachwear that embarrasses the family.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition rather than showing possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A mankini is a skimpy one-piece men's swimsuit, made famous by the film Borat, so it is daring beachwear.

clue.text: Knight with place to sleep after overturning rubble

indicators.note: overturning something turns it upside down, which in a down entry reverses the letters

blocks.note: Sir is the title of a knight
a bed is a place to sleep

explanation.surface: A knight looks for a bed after clambering over heaps of rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the bed second, and 'overturning' then flips the whole string, so the order is reversed as well as the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered broken fragments left after destruction, the same thing as rubble.

clue.text: Support for surfer seen in charge at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means being lost and confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, all twelve letters used

explanation.surface: A lifeguard is seen in charge of helping surfers out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfer here rides the web, not waves, so the support is a tool for finding pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who surfs the internet relies on a search engine like Google to find websites, so it supports their browsing.

clue.text: Celebrity contribution to festival is terrible

indicators.note: a contribution to something is a part of it, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A famous guest's performance at a festival is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across festivAL IS Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of famous people, so it is used attributively for celebrity status.

clue.text: The woman snatching old footwear item

indicators.note: to snatch something is to grab and hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A woman grabs an ancient boot or slipper.
explanation.walkthrough: O for old is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe is an article worn on the foot, a basic footwear item.

clue.text: A sailor going round India, backing Indian dish

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece encloses another
backing means moving backwards, so the letters run in the reverse direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a tar is an old term for a sailor
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A seaman sailing around India comes to back a local dish.
explanation.walkthrough: TAR goes round I to give TIAR, A goes in front, and the whole is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yogurt-based side dish from Indian cuisine, often with cucumber and mint.

clue.text: Massage bishop? Nonsense

blocks.note: a rub is a massage
a jocular clipped form of bishop, the question mark admitting the liberty

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of giving a bishop a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the cheeky shortening of the churchman's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is used informally to mean foolish talk or ideas, exactly as nonsense is.

clue.text: Inferior pop group releasing some number

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a pop group is a band
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A second-rate pop band puts out one of their songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' suggests a song from the band, but it is N, the algebraic symbol for an indefinite number.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bad is poor in quality, below standard, which is what inferior means.

clue.text: Satisfied article not found in what vegetarians decline

indicators.note: something not found in a place is absent from it, so it is removed

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
vegetarians refuse to eat meat

explanation.surface: A contented diner finds no trace of what vegetarians turn down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' means refuse here; MEAT without A gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands or needs that are satisfied have been met, as in fulfilling a requirement.

clue.text: Experimental trip vets tried out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in proper order, so the letters need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written, all nine letters used

explanation.surface: Veterinarians try out an experimental journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tried out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' alone is the signal and 'tried' is letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A test drive is a trial run in a vehicle before buying it, a journey made to try something out.
